title: Synthesis of gold–tin alloy nanoparticles with tunable plasmonic properties
protocol: Weigh 39.4 mg of HAuCl4 trihydrate into a glass scintillation vial.
Add 10 mL of ultrapure water to yield a 10 mM HAuCl4 solution.
Weigh 58.8 mg of trisodium citrate dihydrate into a glass scintillation vial.
Add 2 mL of ultrapure water to yield a 100 mM trisodium citrate solution.
Transfer ultrapure water to a clean 250 mL round bottom flask.
Place a clean 25.4 mm PTFE stir bar into the flask.
Set up a heating mantle and attach it to a heat controller.
Initiate stirring at 640 r.p.m.
Set the heating mantle and attached heat controller to 138°C.
Fasten a condenser to the neck of the round bottom flask.
Turn on water for circulation through the condenser.
Ensure all components are securely attached to a ring stand with minimal motion.
Remove the condenser once the water is boiling and the reaction vessel is visibly at reflux.
Directly pipette the 10 mM HAuCl4 solution into the reaction vessel.
Place the condenser back onto the reaction vessel.
Rapidly pipette the 100 mM trisodium citrate solution in a single injection.
Heat and stir for 8 minutes after re-attaching the condenser.
Prepare a 10 wt.% polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) solution.
Weigh 0.1 g of PVP into a 20 mL clean glass scintillation vial.
Add 1 mL of ultrapure water to the vial and swirl until fully dissolved.
If necessary, sonicate the vial to expedite dissolution.
Prepare a 5 mM SnCl4 solution.
Pipette 7.5 mL of ultrapure water into a clean glass vial.
In a fume hood, add 4.34 μL of SnCl4 rapidly using a micropipette.
Swirl the vial until fully dissolved.
Prepare a 260 mM NaBH4 solution.
Weigh 20 mg of NaBH4 into a clean glass vial.
Add 2.03 mL of ultrapure water immediately before use and swirl until dissolved.
Do not store the 260 mM NaBH4 solution for future use.
Pipette 6 mL of as-synthesized Au seeds into a clean glass vial.
Add a 12.7 mm PTFE stir bar to the vial.
Place the vials back on the stir plates and begin stirring at 1,500 rpm.
Pipette the 10 wt.% PVP solution into the vial.
Add the 5 mM SnCl4 solution to the vial immediately after adding the PVP.
Remove the reaction vials from the stir plates and cap them.
Place the capped vials into a hot water bath at 60°C for 10 minutes.
Uncover the vials and place back on the stir plates, resuming stirring.
Pipette the freshly prepared 260 mM NaBH4 solution to the vials.
The solution should change to a translucent, homogeneous yellow-orange color with residual bubble formation.
Allow the solution to stir for 30 seconds.
Remove the reaction vials from the stir plates and cover them again.
Place the covered vials back into the hot water bath at 60°C for 20 minutes.
Remove the vials from the 60°C hot water bath.
Remove the 12.7 mm PTFE stir bars from the sample solutions with the assistance of another stir bar upon removal from the hot water bath.
Allow colloidal suspensions to return to room temperature before characterizing.
Perform background and blank correction using ultrapure water pipetted directly into the quartz cuvette.
Pipette samples prepared in Step 4 directly into a clean 1 cm path-length quartz cuvette without dilution or concentration of the colloid.
Measure the UV-visible spectrum over a range of 200–700 nm.
Ensure data is appropriately saved on your device.
Pipette samples into 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Place the tubes into a centrifuge.
Centrifuge samples at 8,000 r.p.m. (5,510 r.c.f.) for 8 minutes.
Carefully remove supernatant and leave the pellet.
Add 1.5 mL of ultrapure water to re-suspend the pellet.
Invert microcentrifuge tubes to ensure even distribution.
Centrifuge samples again at 8,000 r.p.m. (5,510 r.c.f.) for 8 minutes.
Carefully remove supernatant, leaving only the concentrated sample in each tube.
Pipette concentrated sample onto a zero-background silicon holder.
Place samples into a desiccator to visibly dry uncovered.
Measure diffraction pattern at a scan rate of 1° min-1 in the 2θ range 10–90° using Rigaku Miniflex X-ray diffractometer.
Pipette samples into 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes and place into centrifuge.
Centrifuge samples at 8,000 r.p.m. (5,510 r.c.f.) for 8 min.
Carefully remove the supernatant after centrifugation.
Re-suspend the concentrated sample back to 1.5 mL by adding ultrapure water.
Ensure sample is evenly distributed by inverting the microcentrifuge tubes.
Place the washed samples back into the centrifuge for another centrifugation at 8,000 r.p.m. (5,510 r.c.f.) for 8 min.
Carefully remove the supernatant again after centrifugation.
Pipette 10 μL of the concentrated sample onto a Ted Pella Cu Carbon Type-B TEM grid.
Allow samples to dry completely in a desiccator uncovered for approximately 2 h.
Bimetallic nanoparticles were imaged using a 100 kV accelerating voltage and ImageJ software for size and polydispersity analysis.
Ensure all imaging and data is saved appropriately for future analysis.
